definition_zh: 螺旋桨；推进器；推动者
definition_en: a device with two or more blades that spin and drive a boat or aircraft forward, or a person who pushes an idea or plan along
core_image: 两片叶片在船尾飞速旋转，把水向后推，船身随之向前
scene: 清晨的湖面上，一艘小艇还没完全发动，船尾的叶片在空气里慢慢转动。The old ferry has a single propeller and a wooden deck.
sceneCN: 这里 propeller 是「螺旋桨」（第 1 个义项：船舶或飞机的旋转推进装置）；句意为这艘老渡轮只有一个螺旋桨和一层木甲板。

pos.zh: 名词：螺旋桨；推进器；推动者

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「推进；推动」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「推进；推进力」
同族名词，义为「推进剂；火箭燃料」

senses.title: A spinning blade assembly for ships and aircraft
senses.titleCN: 船舶与飞机的旋转推进装置
senses.definition: a set of angled blades mounted on a shaft that turn fast and push water or air backwards
senses.definitionCN: 装在一根轴上的一组带角度的叶片，高速旋转把水或空气向后推
senses.example: A fishing net had caught on the ferry propeller.
senses.exampleCN: 一张渔网缠在了渡轮的螺旋桨上。
senses.why: The Latin verb propellere means to drive forward, and the -er ending names the thing that does the driving, so the propeller is the pushing agent made of metal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 propellere 意为向前推进，-er 后缀指执行这个动作的东西，于是 propeller 就是那个由金属制成的「推动者」。

senses.title: The propelling part of any machine
senses.titleCN: 通用推进器：机器中负责前进的部件
senses.definition: any rotating or moving part whose job is to turn engine power into forward movement
senses.definitionCN: 任何把发动机动力转成向前运动的旋转或运动部件
senses.example: The motor in the model boat turned a small plastic propeller.
senses.exampleCN: 模型船里的马达带动一个小小的塑料推进器。
senses.why: Once the word meant the part that drives rather than the whole craft, it spread to toy boats, drones and fans.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词从「整条船」转指「负责推动作用的那一部件」，它就扩散到玩具船、无人机和风扇上。

senses.title: Someone who pushes things along
senses.titleCN: 推动者：把事情推向前的人
senses.definition: a person whose energy and effort move an idea, project or campaign forward
senses.definitionCN: 凭精力与努力把想法、项目或活动推向前的人
senses.example: She was the propeller behind the school garden project.
senses.exampleCN: 她是学校菜园项目背后的推动者。
senses.why: The physical blade pushing water becomes a metaphor for a person pushing work along, with the same forward-driving root.
senses.whyCN: 推动水的叶片被比作推着工作向前的人，靠的是同一个「向前驱赶」的词根。

intro.en: Propeller comes from Latin propellere, to drive forward, through the English verb propel plus the agent suffix -er. The word for the spinning device appeared in the nineteenth century with screw propulsion.
intro.cn: propeller 来自拉丁语 propellere（向前推进），经由英语动词 propel 加施动者后缀 -er 构成；指旋转装置的用法在十九世纪随螺旋推进技术出现。

items.en: Pellere means to drive or push, and pro- adds forward, giving propellere, to drive forward.
items.cn: pellere 意为驱赶、推，pro- 加上「向前」，构成 propellere（向前推进）。

items.en: The participle propellens, driving forward, shows the -ent- stem that English later reshaped.
items.cn: 分词 propellens（向前推进的）显示出 -ent- 词干，英语后来把它改造成自己的形式。

items.en: The verb propel enters English as a learned borrowing for pushing something forward.
items.cn: 动词 propel 作为书面借词进入英语，表示把某物向前推。

items.en: Propeller is coined for the screw-shaped blade that drives steamships and then aircraft.
items.cn: propeller 被用来命名推动蒸汽船、后来又推动飞机的螺旋桨。

items.en: The word spreads to fans, turbines, toy boats and, figuratively, to people who drive projects.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到风扇、涡轮机、玩具船，也比喻性地指推动项目的人。

note.en: Propeller is the agent noun of propel, sharing the pellere family, and it belongs with the words that describe how vehicles move through water or air.
note.cn: propeller 是 propel 的施动者名词，属于 pellere 词族，并与描述交通工具如何在水中或空中前进的词同场。

entries.definition: to push something forward
entries.definitionCN: 推动；推进

entries.definition: a substance that drives something forward
entries.definitionCN: 推进剂；同根的后缀 -ant 指物质而非部件

entries.definition: a substance that drives things away
entries.definitionCN: 驱避剂；与 propeller 拼写相近，但 re- 表示向后赶

entries.definition: a machine driven by fluid turning blades
entries.definitionCN: 由流体推动叶片而转动的涡轮机

entries.definition: the rotating part of a machine
entries.definitionCN: 机器的旋转部件

entries.definition: a short pole with a flat blade used to move a small boat
entries.definitionCN: 划小船用的短桨

normalIntro.en: Propeller is propel plus -er: the one that pushes. Its pellere family includes expel, repel and propeller itself.
normalIntro.cn: propeller 是 propel 加 -er：负责推的那个东西；pellere 词族还有 expel、repel 等词。

normal.en: Read it as propel plus -er, the agent that drives the boat forward.
normal.cn: 把它读成 propel 加 -er，即推动船前进的那个装置。

normal.en: A propeller blade is angled so that spinning turns into forward thrust.
normal.cn: 螺旋桨叶片是带角度的，旋转因此变成向前的推力。

normal.en: The propeller shaft links the engine to the blades.
normal.cn: propeller shaft 把发动机和叶片连接起来。

normal.en: Propeller-driven aircraft fly more slowly and cheaply than jets.
normal.cn: 螺旋桨驱动的飞机比喷气机飞得慢也更省钱。

normal.en: Repel and expel share the pellere root but point back and out, not forward.
normal.cn: repel 与 expel 共享 pellere 词根，但方向是向后、向外，而不是向前。

abstract.en: Picture the white wake spreading behind a boat as its blades turn.
abstract.cn: 想象叶片转动时船后拖开的白色尾迹。

abstract.en: Hear the low hum of a propeller plane fading over the field.
abstract.cn: 听一听螺旋桨小飞机在田野上空渐渐远去的低鸣。

abstract.en: See a hand spinning a toy paddle and feeling the push of air.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手转动玩具桨叶，感到气流被推开。

examples.en: The propeller of the small plane stopped turning for a second.
examples.cn: 小飞机的螺旋桨停转了一秒。

examples.en: Divers cleared seaweed from both propellers before the crossing.
examples.cn: 渡海前潜水员清除了两个螺旋桨上的海草。

examples.en: He has been the main propeller of the cleanup campaign.
examples.cn: 他一直是这场清洁运动的主要推动者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若了」——船桨一扑、叶轮一转，船就往前走；这只是读音联想，与词源无关（真实词源见 propellere 加 -er）。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ pellere（驱赶）→ propellere（向前推）→ 英语 propel（推进）→ propeller（施动者名词，推动的装置）。同族 expel、repel 保留了方向相反的「推、赶」。

sensesIntro.en: Propeller first names the spinning blade device, then any propelling part of a machine, and finally, by metaphor, a person who pushes work forward.
sensesIntro.cn: propeller 先指旋转的叶片装置，再泛指机器中负责推进的部件，最后比喻把事情推向前的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: blades turning in water and throwing it back so the boat moves ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：叶片在水中转动，把水向后抛，船于是向前。

branches.en: The concrete blade assembly on ships and aircraft is the first sense.
branches.cn: 船与飞机上具体的叶片组件是第一个义项。

branches.en: Any machine part that turns power into movement is the general sense.
branches.cn: 任何把动力转成运动的机器部件是泛指义项。

branches.en: A person who drives a project borrows the blade image.
branches.cn: 推动项目的人借用了叶片的比喻。

branches.en: Both the ferry blade and the toy part do the same pushing job.
branches.cn: 渡轮叶片与玩具部件干的都是同一件推进的活。

branches.en: A propelling part and a driving person both convert effort into forward motion.
branches.cn: 推进部件与推动者都把努力变成向前的运动。

intro.en: Propeller is built from the Latin verb pellere with the prefixes pro- and the agent suffix -er; the family shows the pushing root under different directions.
intro.cn: propeller 由拉丁语动词 pellere 加上前缀 pro- 与施动者后缀 -er 构成，整个词族在不同方向上体现同一个「推」的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin pellere means to drive, pro- means forward, and the -er suffix marks the doer of the action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pellere 意为驱赶，pro- 意为向前，-er 后缀标明动作的执行者。

items.example: Pellere supplies the pushing root.
items.exampleCN: pellere 提供「推」的词根。

items.example: The prefix pro- gives the forward direction.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 给出向前的方向。

items.example: Propellere is the source of the whole English set.
items.exampleCN: propellere 是整组英语词的来源。

items.example: The suffix -er turns propel into propeller.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把 propel 变成 propeller。

items.example: Propel is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: propel 是这个名词背后的动词。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms propulsion.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 propulsion。

items.example: Expel sends the push outward.
items.exampleCN: expel 把推力朝外。

items.example: Repel sends the push backward.
items.exampleCN: repel 把推力朝后。

items.example: Impel pushes inward as an inner urge.
items.exampleCN: impel 向内推，表示内心的驱使。

latinEntries.meaning: to drive into or urge on

definition_zh: 倾向；习性；癖好
definition_en: a natural or strong tendency to behave in a particular way or to prefer a particular thing
core_image: 身体不自觉地朝一侧倾斜，像被看不见的手轻轻推着
scene: 深夜的厨房里，桌上的点心还没收走，一个人又伸手去拿。He has a propensity to snack while he works.
sceneCN: 这里 propensity 是「倾向、习性」（第 1 个义项：自然或强烈的行为倾向）；句意为他工作时有吃零食的习性。

pos.zh: 名词：倾向；习性；癖好

collocations.zh: 对……有倾向（尤指不良习性）

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「倾向的；有意向的」，现已少用
由同一分词加 -ion 构成的名词，义为「倾向」，多见于早期文本
由拉丁语 propensus 加形容词后缀构成，义为「倾向的；偏好的」

senses.title: A natural leaning toward a habit
senses.definition: a built-in tendency to act in a certain way, often used for a habit others disapprove of
senses.definitionCN: 一种天生的、以某种方式行事的倾向，常指别人不赞成的习性
senses.example: Children have a natural propensity to imitate adults.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子有模仿大人的天性。
senses.why: Latin propensus is the participle of propendere, to hang forward, from pro-, forward, and pendere, to hang; a propensity is a mind leaning over in one direction.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 propensus 是 propendere（向前悬垂）的分词，由 pro-（向前）与 pendere（悬挂）构成；propensity 就是心智朝某个方向倾过去。

senses.title: A liking for a kind of thing
senses.definition: a leaning toward a particular activity, food, risk or style that one enjoys
senses.definitionCN: 对某种活动、食物、风险或风格的偏好
senses.example: Her propensity for spicy food started in childhood.
senses.exampleCN: 她爱吃辣的偏好从童年就开始了。
senses.why: The same leaning image applies to pleasure as well as habit: the mind tips toward what it likes.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「倾斜」的画面也适用于喜好：心智会朝自己喜欢的东西偏过去。

senses.title: A statistical tendency in a group
senses.definition: the average rate at which members of a group do something, used in economics and social science
senses.definitionCN: 群体成员做某事的一般比例，用于经济学与社会科学
senses.example: Younger consumers show a higher propensity to spend online.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻消费者在网上消费的倾向更高。
senses.why: When economists measure how a whole population leans in one direction, the personal leaning becomes a statistical rate.
senses.whyCN: 当经济学家衡量整群人朝某方向倾斜的程度时，个人的倾向就变成了统计比例。

intro.en: Propensity comes from Latin propensus, inclined or leaning forward, the participle of propendere, to hang forward. It entered English as a learned word for a natural leaning of the mind.
intro.cn: propensity 来自拉丁语 propensus（倾向的、向前倾斜的），是 propendere（向前悬垂）的分词；它作为书面词进入英语，指心智的自然倾向。

items.en: Pendere means to hang or weigh, and pro- adds forward, giving propendere, to hang forward.
items.cn: pendere 意为悬挂、称重，加上 pro-（向前）得到 propendere，即向前悬垂。

items.en: The participle propensus describes something that leans or is inclined toward a side.
items.cn: 分词 propensus 描述朝一侧倾斜或偏向的事物。

items.en: Scholastic and later Latin uses the noun propensitas for a leaning or disposition, built on the participle.
items.cn: 经院哲学与后世拉丁语用名词 propensitas 表示倾斜或性情，其基础是这一分词。

items.en: English borrows the word as propensity, first for a leaning of the body and then of the mind.
items.cn: 英语借入该词写作 propensity，最初指身体倾斜，继而指心智倾向。

items.en: The Latin noun propensitas explains the -ity ending, and the term later becomes standard in economics and statistics.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 propensitas 解释了 -ity 词尾的来源；这个词后来在经济学与统计学中成为标准术语。

note.en: Propensity is built on the pendere family of hanging and weighing words, and it sits close to tendency, inclination and leaning.
note.cn: propensity 建立在 pendere「悬挂、称量」词族之上，并与 tendency、inclination、leaning 等词相邻。

entries.definition: inclined or disposed by nature
entries.definitionCN: 天生倾向的；现较少使用

entries.definition: a hanging ornament
entries.definitionCN: 悬挂的饰物；同根于「悬挂」

entries.definition: a regular payment after retirement
entries.definitionCN: 退休金；同根于「称量、付出」，但含义不同

entries.definition: a general likelihood of behaving in a certain way
entries.definitionCN: 一般性的行为趋势

entries.definition: a feeling of wanting to do something
entries.definitionCN: 想要做某事的意向

entries.definition: a preference for one side or opinion
entries.definitionCN: 对某一方或某种看法的偏好

normalIntro.en: Propensity carries the Latin pendere, to hang; the same hanging root sits in pendant, pendant and pendulum.
normalIntro.cn: propensity 带着拉丁语 pendere「悬挂」的意思，同一个悬挂词根也出现在 pendant 与 pendulum 等词里。

normal.en: Split it as pro- plus pens plus -ity: leaning forward is the picture.
normal.cn: 拆成 pro- 加 pens 加 -ity：向前倾就是它的画面。

normal.en: Use for with a noun and to with a verb: a propensity for risk, a propensity to overspend.
normal.cn: 名词后接 for，动词前用 to：风险偏好、容易超支的倾向。

normal.en: It usually carries a slight tone of criticism; enthusiasm is better praise.
normal.cn: 它通常略带批评意味，夸奖时用 enthusiasm 更合适。

normal.en: Pendulum swings because it hangs from a fixed point, the same hanging idea.
normal.cn: pendulum（钟摆）因为挂在固定点上才摆动，正是同一个悬挂概念。

normal.en: Economists speak of the propensity to consume, a measured rate of spending.
normal.cn: 经济学家说消费倾向，那就是一个被测量出来的支出比例。

abstract.en: Picture a tired man leaning toward a plate of biscuits without noticing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个疲倦的人不自觉地朝饼干盘倾斜身体。

abstract.en: See a compass needle turning toward north again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象磁针一次又一次地转向北方。

abstract.en: Think of a rope hanging slightly to one side, pulled by an unseen weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子被看不见的重物拉着，稍稍偏向一侧。

examples.en: Some people have a propensity to exaggerate under pressure.
examples.cn: 有些人在压力下容易夸张。

examples.en: Researchers measured the propensity of consumers to save.
examples.cn: 研究人员测量了消费者的储蓄倾向。

examples.en: His propensity for taking risks worried the board.
examples.cn: 他爱冒险的倾向让董事会感到担忧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑奔寺」——身体不由地扑向某个地方，像被一股劲推着走，这就是倾向；这只是读音联想，与词源无关（真实词源见 propendere）。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ pendere（悬挂、称量）→ propendere（向前悬垂）→ propensus（倾斜的）→ propensity（倾向）。核心是「向前倾」，同族 pendant、pendulum 保留「悬挂」。

sensesIntro.en: Propensity begins with a personal leaning, widens to a liking for particular things, and ends with a statistical tendency measured across groups.
sensesIntro.cn: propensity 先指个人的倾斜倾向，扩大为对特定事物的偏好，最后指在群体层面测量出的统计倾向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body tilting to one side, pulled by an unseen weight.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体被看不见的重物拉着，朝一侧倾斜。

branches.en: A built-in leaning toward a habit is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 天生偏向某种行为是日常义项。

branches.en: Leaning toward something pleasant gives the liking sense.
branches.cn: 朝令人愉快的事物倾斜产生偏好义。

branches.en: A measured rate for a whole group is the statistical sense.
branches.cn: 针对整群人的测量比例是统计义项。

branches.en: Habit and liking often point in the same direction of the mind.
branches.cn: 习性与偏好往往是心智朝同一方向倾斜。

branches.en: Individual leanings, added up, become the propensity of a population.
branches.cn: 个人的倾斜累加起来，就成为一个群体的倾向。

intro.en: Propensity is built from the Latin prefix pro-, the root pendere, and the noun suffix -ity, with the hanging family of pendant and pendulum behind it.
intro.cn: propensity 由拉丁语前缀 pro-、词根 pendere 与名词后缀 -ity 构成，背后是 pendant、pendulum 的「悬挂」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere means to hang or weigh, pro- means forward, and the noun of quality ends in -tas, which English reshaped as -ity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 意为悬挂、称量，pro- 意为向前，性质名词以 -tas 结尾，英语改写为 -ity。

items.example: Pendere supplies the hanging root.
items.exampleCN: pendere 提供「悬挂」的词根。

items.example: The prefix pro- points the leaning forward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 把倾斜的方向指向前方。

items.example: Propensus describes a leaning rather than a fall.
items.exampleCN: propensus 描述的是倾斜，而不是倒下。

items.example: The suffix -ity turns the participle into a noun of quality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 把分词变成性质名词。

items.example: Propensity keeps the core leaning image.
items.exampleCN: propensity 保留核心的倾斜意象。

items.example: A pendulum hangs from a fixed point and swings.
items.exampleCN: 钟摆挂在固定点上并来回摆动。

items.example: A pendant hangs from a chain.
items.exampleCN: 吊坠挂在链子上。

items.example: Append means hanging something onto the end.
items.exampleCN: append 表示把东西挂到末尾。

items.meaning: to weigh out or use up
items.example: Expend comes from weighing out money.
items.exampleCN: expend 源自把钱财称量付出。

definition_zh: 业主；所有人；经营者（尤指小企业老板）
definition_en: the person who owns a business, a property or a hotel, especially when that person runs it as well
core_image: 一块刻着某人名字的招牌，挂在他自己经营的店门上方
scene: 小镇街角的面包店开了三十多年，招牌一直没换，店里的人换了一茬又一茬。The proprietor still unlocks the door himself every morning at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 proprietor 是「业主、店主人」（第 1 个义项：拥有并亲自经营店铺或旅舍的人）；句意：店主每天清晨仍然亲自开门。画面里能看到旧招牌、门锁和热腾腾的面包。

pos.zh: 名词：所有人；业主；经营者；旅店老板

collocations.zh: 独资经营者；个体工商户

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀构成，义为「专有的；专利的；业主拥有的」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「所有权；业主身份；独资经营」
由本词加词尾构成，义为「业主的；所有者的」
同出拉丁词 proprius（自己的），义为「得体；适当」，与 proprietor 并非直接派生

senses.title: The owner of a business
senses.definition: the owner of a shop, hotel, restaurant or small business, especially one who runs it personally
senses.definitionCN: 店铺、旅店、餐馆或小企业的所有人，尤指亲自经营者
senses.example: The proprietor greets customers at the door of the bakery.
senses.exampleCN: 店主在面包店门口迎接顾客。
senses.why: Latin proprius meant one own, and the suffix -or marks the person: proprietor names whoever holds the shop as his or her own.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proprius 意为「自己的」，后缀 -or 指「人」：proprietor 就是把这间店铺视为己有的人。

senses.title: The owner of land or a property
senses.definition: the legal owner of a building, a piece of land or some other property
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物、土地或其他财产的合法所有人
senses.example: The proprietor of the land refused to sell it to developers.
senses.exampleCN: 这块土地的所有人拒绝把地卖给开发商。
senses.why: Ownership is the core idea, so any thing that can be owned, land and houses included, can have a proprietor.
senses.whyCN: 所有权是核心含义，因此任何可以拥有的东西，包括土地和房屋，都可以有 proprietor。

senses.title: A hotel or guesthouse keeper
senses.definition: the person who owns and takes care of a small hotel or a guesthouse
senses.definitionCN: 拥有并亲自经营小旅馆或家庭客栈的人
senses.example: The proprietor of the seaside guesthouse cooks breakfast for every guest.
senses.exampleCN: 海边客栈的老板给每位客人做早饭。
senses.why: Small inns were long family businesses, so the owner and the host were the same person, and proprietor took on that hosting sense.
senses.whyCN: 小旅馆长期是家族生意，东家与招待是同一个人，proprietor 因而带上这种东道主的意味。

senses.title: Sole proprietor
senses.definition: in the phrase sole proprietor, a business owned and managed by one person, who is personally responsible for its debts
senses.definitionCN: 用于 sole proprietor，指由一人拥有并经营、并亲自承担债务的企业主
senses.example: As a sole proprietor, she files her business income on her own tax return.
senses.exampleCN: 作为独资经营者，她在自己的税表上申报经营收入。
senses.why: Law needs a clear single holder of rights and duties, so proprietor became the standard word for the one person behind an unincorporated firm.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要有明确的单一权利义务主体，proprietor 于是成了非法人企业中那个唯一主人身上的标准用词。

senses.title: The holder of a right or title
senses.titleCN: 权利持有人；登记产权人
senses.definition: the person in whose name a right, a licence or a registered title is legally held
senses.definitionCN: 权利、执照或已登记产权在法律上登记在其名下的人
senses.example: The registered proprietor of the trademark must approve any change of name.
senses.exampleCN: 商标的登记产权人必须同意任何名称变更。
senses.why: Latin proprietas named the holding of a thing as one own, so the word can also personify a legal title that sits in someone name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proprietas 指把某物视为己有的状态，因此这个词也能用来指代落在某人名下的法律权属。

senses.title: Figurative owner of an idea
senses.definition: in literary style, the person or thing that seems to own a quality, a place or a way of behaving
senses.definitionCN: 文学性用法：看似拥有某种品质、某地或某种作风的人或事物
senses.example: Frost is the proprietor of the winter garden, ruling every leaf on the hedge.
senses.exampleCN: 寒霜是冬园的主人，管着篱笆上的每一片叶子。
senses.why: The noun of ownership is stretched into metaphor: whoever dominates a scene is pictured as holding the deed to it.
senses.whyCN: 表示所有权的名词被拉进比喻：谁主导了一处场景，谁就被想象成握着那块地方的地契。

intro.en: Proprietor joins a Latin adjective for own with a Latin person suffix, and the whole family gathers around the idea of holding something as ones own.
intro.cn: proprietor 由拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词加上指人的后缀构成，整个词族都围绕「把某物视为己有」的概念。

items.en: The adjective proprius meant own, individual, belonging to oneself as opposed to common, and it also gave the noun proprietas, ownership.
items.cn: 形容词 proprius 意为「自己的、个人的」，与「公共的」相对，还生出名词 proprietas「所有权」。

items.en: Proprietarius named a person who owns property, formed from proprietas with the person suffix -arius.
items.cn: proprietarius 由 proprietas 加指人后缀 -arius 构成，指拥有财产的人。

items.en: The form was taken into French, where -aire replaced -arius, giving proprietaire; the English spelling follows the Latin suffix -or more than the French one.
items.cn: 该词形进入法语后，以 -aire 替换了 -arius，成为 proprietaire；英语拼写更多沿用拉丁语指人后缀 -or。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the sixteenth century, first in legal writing about land and then about shops and inns.
items.cn: 名词在英语中十六世纪已有记录，最早见于关于土地的法律文书，后来用于店铺和旅店。

items.en: Booksellers and newspaper owners were long called proprietors, while the phrase sole proprietor fixed the word in company law. The exact first date of the English word is uncertain.
items.cn: 书商与报馆老板长期被称作 proprietor，sole proprietor 这一说法又把该词固定在公司法中。英语首见的确切年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin root for own; the near-meaning group gathers the people and documents of ownership.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根「自己的」构成的词语；近义组收与所有权有关的人和文书。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning owned privately or used exclusively, as in proprietary software.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「专有的、私有的」，如 proprietary software 专有软件。

entries.definition: The state or business form of being an owner, as in sole proprietorship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「所有权、业主身份」，如 sole proprietorship 独资企业。

entries.definition: An older feminine form for a woman who owns a business or property.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，旧时指女店主、女业主。

entries.definition: Correctness of behaviour, from the same Latin root but a different branch of meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「得体、规矩」，同出拉丁词根，但属于另一支含义。

entries.definition: To win favour by pleasing; only it looks similar, because its root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「安抚、取悦」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The general everyday word for a person who owns something; broader and plainer than proprietor.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「所有者」，最普通宽泛的日常说法，比 proprietor 平淡。

entries.definition: Formal or business style for an owner, especially one who runs a small shop or inn.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小店老板」，英国英语中的日常说法，兼有 proprietor 的「店主」义。

entries.definition: The owner of a house or flat who rents it out to others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「房东」，把房屋出租给他人的人。

entries.definition: The person named on a title deed as the legal owner of a property.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指产权证上登记的合法房产所有人。

entries.definition: A person or firm that holds a licence to run a business in a place owned by someone else.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「特许经营者」，在他人场地内持有经营许可经营生意的人或公司。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root, the ordinary phrases and the legal pairs the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根、这个词实际出现的常见搭配，以及它在法律中的常见对照组。

normal.en: proprius means own, so a proprietor is the one for whom the shop is own.
normal.cn: proprius 意为「自己的」，proprietor 就是这家店归属的那个人。

normal.en: The suffix -or names a person, as in actor, director and proprietor.
normal.cn: 后缀 -or 表示「人」，actor、director 与 proprietor 都是这样。

normal.en: A sole proprietor owns the whole business and carries its debts alone.
normal.cn: sole proprietor 拥有整门生意，也独自承担它的债务。

normal.en: A landlord owns a house to let; a proprietor usually runs the place as well.
normal.cn: landlord 拥有出租的房屋；proprietor 通常还亲自经营。

normal.en: proprietary marks what is owned, proprietorship marks the owning, proprietor marks the owner.
normal.cn: proprietary 标出「被拥有的」，proprietorship 标出「拥有这件事」，proprietor 标出「所有者」。

abstract.en: Picture a carved sign above a bakery door, with the name of the person inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象面包店门上方的木刻招牌，招牌里刻着店主的名字。

abstract.en: Picture the same name on a title deed for a field far from any shop.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个名字也写在远处一块田地的产权证上。

abstract.en: Picture the owner serving breakfast to guests in the kitchen of a small inn.
abstract.cn: 想象小旅馆的东家亲自在厨房给客人做早饭。

examples.en: The proprietor of the bookshop lives in the flat above it.
examples.cn: 书店的老板就住在店上面的公寓里。

examples.en: She became the sole proprietor of the family firm in two thousand and ten.
examples.cn: 她在二零一零年成为家族公司的唯一所有人。

examples.en: The new proprietor plans to repaint the old hotel without changing its name.
examples.cn: 新老板打算重新粉刷这家老旅馆，但不改它的名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼普瑞艾特」——泼一泼招牌上的灰，普瑞老板站在门口迎客；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 proprius（自己的）+ -etor/-or（指人后缀）→ 中世纪拉丁语 proprietarius（财产所有人）→ 法语 proprietaire → 英语 proprietor，核心义「把某物视为己有的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Proprietor begins with the owner who runs a shop, widens to legal owners of land and rights, then turns into a metaphor for whoever dominates a scene.
sensesIntro.cn: proprietor 从亲自经营店铺的店主起，扩展到土地与权利的合法所有人，最后演化为形容谁主宰一处场景的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carved sign above a shop door carries the name of the person who owns the place.
core.cn: 核心意象：店门上方的木刻招牌上，刻着拥有这家店的人的名字。

branches.en: THE SHOP: ownership plus personal running gives the everyday business sense.
branches.cn: 店铺线：所有权加上亲自经营，构成日常的商业义。

branches.en: THE DEED: any building or piece of land has a proprietor named in law.
branches.cn: 地契线：任何房屋或土地在法律上都有登记的 proprietor。

branches.en: THE INN: the host of a small hotel is also its owner, so the word names the keeper.
branches.cn: 旅舍线：小旅馆的东家同时是房主，于是这个词也指旅舍老板。

branches.en: THE LAW: sole proprietor and registered proprietor fix the owner as the single holder of duties and rights.
branches.cn: 法律线：sole proprietor 与 registered proprietor 把所有人固定为权利与义务的单一主体。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: whoever dominates a place is pictured as holding its deed.
branches.cn: 比喻线：谁主宰一处场景，谁就被想象成握着那块地方的地契。

intro.en: Proprietor is a Latin root plus a Latin person suffix, and English adds ordinary suffixes to build the family.
intro.cn: proprietor 由一个拉丁词根与一个拉丁指人后缀组成，英语再用普通后缀扩展出这个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin has both proprius, own, and proprietas, ownership, so only the deeper Indo-European form is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中既有 proprius「自己的」，也有 proprietas「所有权」，只有更早的印欧语词形属于重构。

items.example: The adjective gives the sense of belonging to oneself.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供「属于自己的」这层含义。

items.example: The abstract noun names the state of owning.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词指「拥有」的状态。

items.example: Medieval Latin add it to make proprietarius.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语加上它构成 proprietarius。

items.example: The suffix marks the owner as a person, not a thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把所有人标记为一个人，而不是一件东西。

items.example: It forms proprietary.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 proprietary。

items.example: It forms proprietorship.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 proprietorship。

items.example: It forms the older word proprietress.
items.exampleCN: 它构成较旧的形式 proprietress。

items.example: It forms proprietorial.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 proprietorial。

items.example: Proprietary software belongs to one company.
items.exampleCN: proprietary software 指归一家公司所有的软件。

items.example: A sole proprietorship has one owner.
items.exampleCN: sole proprietorship 指独资经营。

latinEntries.meaning: to give as own, to appropriate

definition_zh: 预期的；有望成为的；未来的；潜在的
definition_en: expected or likely to happen or to become something in the future, but not yet actual
core_image: 一条伸向前方的路，尽头有一座尚未抵达的房子
scene: 招聘会开在体育馆里，学生们拿着简历在展位前排成长队，几家公司的招聘牌上都写着欢迎新同事。Hundreds of prospective employees queued with copies of their CVs.
sceneCN: 这里 prospective 是「有望成为的、未来的」（第 1 个义项：有可能将来成为某身份的人）；句意：几百名准员工带着自己的简历排队。画面里有排队的人群、展位和写满岗位的招聘牌。

pos.zh: 形容词：预期的；未来的；有望成为的；潜在的

collocations.zh: 准新生；有意报考的学生

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词根构成的基础名词，义为「前景；可能性」，prospective 由它派生
由同一词根加后缀构成，义为「勘探者」，指寻觅矿藏 prospects 的人
同出拉丁 specere（看），义为「视角；透视」，与 prospective 同根不同义
由本词词根加后缀构成，义为「远景观测；预测」，较少用

senses.title: Expected to become something
senses.definition: likely to become a particular thing or to take a particular role, as in a prospective student or a prospective buyer
senses.definitionCN: 有可能成为某种身份或担任某种角色的，如准学生、潜在买家
senses.example: Prospective buyers were invited to view the house on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 潜在买家受邀在周日看房。
senses.why: Latin specere means to look, and pro- means forward: a prospective person is someone the mind looks at as a possible future member.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 specere 意为「看」，pro- 意为「向前」：prospective 的人是我们在心里往前看时预想的未来一员。

senses.title: Expected to happen
senses.definition: likely or planned to take place in the future, usually in the phrase prospective changes or prospective benefits
senses.definitionCN: 在未来可能或计划发生的，常用于 prospective changes、prospective benefits 等说法
senses.example: The company announced prospective changes to its pension scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 公司宣布了对养老金方案预期将作出的调整。
senses.why: Something that is expected sits at the far end of the forward look: it is not here yet, but it is already in sight.
senses.whyCN: 预期之事位于向前看的最远端：它还没到来，却已经出现在视野里。

senses.title: Future in a legal or formal context
senses.definition: existing with regard to the future, as in a prospective law or a prospective owner, as opposed to retrospective
senses.definitionCN: 针对未来而存在的，如将来才生效的法律或未来的所有人，与「追溯既往」相对
senses.example: The new licensing rules are prospective and apply only to applications made next year.
senses.exampleCN: 新的许可规则只管将来的情况，只适用于明年递交的申请。
senses.why: Legal talk points the sense of looking forward at time itself: what is prospective exists only after the rule begins to act.
senses.whyCN: 法律用语把「向前看」对准时间本身：prospective 的东西只在规则生效之后才存在。

senses.title: Potential: not yet actual
senses.definition: possible but not yet real, said of people, clients or results that may exist later
senses.definitionCN: 可能但尚未成真，用于将来可能出现的人、客户或结果
senses.example: The team drew up a list of prospective clients in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 团队列出了该地区的潜在客户名单。
senses.why: The forward view can also be a list of candidates: people who are not clients yet are watched as possible future ones.
senses.whyCN: 向前看也可以变成一份候选名单：还不是客户的人被当作未来的客户来打量。

senses.title: Seen in prospect
senses.definition: in formal or literary style, viewed with regard to what may come, as in prospective profits or a prospective view
senses.definitionCN: 正式或文学用法：从可能到来的角度去看的，如预期利润、前瞻视野
senses.example: The report weighs the prospective profits of the scheme against its risks.
senses.exampleCN: 报告权衡了该方案的预期利润与风险。
senses.why: Formal style keeps the original image of a view: the writer compares gains from where they stand, looking ahead.
senses.whyCN: 正式语体保留了「视野」的原始意象：作者站在当下，朝前比较可能到来的收益。

intro.en: Prospective is built from a Latin prefix for forward and a Latin verb for looking, and it names whatever the mind sees ahead.
intro.cn: prospective 由表示「向前」的拉丁前缀和表示「看」的拉丁动词构成，指心里向前看到的那些事物。

items.en: *spek- is generally reconstructed as to look, to observe, and it underlies Latin specere and Greek skopein.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *spek- 表示「看、观察」，它是拉丁语 specere 与希腊语 skopein 的来源。

items.en: Specere meant to look or to observe, and it gave speculator, a watchman, and species, an appearance.
items.cn: specere 意为「看、观察」，它生出 speculator「守望者」与 species「外貌」。

items.en: Pro plus spectus, a looking, formed prospectus, a view or an outlook, which was also used of a place that offers a wide view.
items.cn: pro 与 spectus「看」合成 prospectus，意为「眺望、远景」，也用来指能望见广阔景色的地方。

items.en: The adjective prospectivus meant related to looking forward or to the view; this is the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: 形容词 prospectivus 意为「与向前看或远景有关的」，它是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.en: The word enters English in the sixteenth century first in optics and then with the modern sense of expected. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 该词十六世纪进入英语，先在光学中使用，后来带上现代的「预期」义。确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb for looking; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what has not yet happened.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语「看」的动词构成的词；近义组收表示「尚未发生」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for a possibility or an outlook, especially the likelihood of future success.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「前景、可能性」，尤指未来成功的可能。

entries.definition: The way things are seen, or the art of showing depth; from the same root but a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「视角、透视」，同根但前缀不同。

entries.definition: Looking back on the past, with the opposite prefix to prospective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「回顾的、追溯的」，前缀与 prospective 相反。

entries.definition: Quick to notice and understand; built on the same verb for seeing through.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有洞察力的」，由同一「看穿」词根构成。

entries.definition: To guess or to invest on a hope; the Latin verb for looking also lies behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推测、投机」，背后也是拉丁语「看」的动词。

entries.definition: Possible but not yet actual; close to prospective and often used of qualities.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「潜在的」，与 prospective 很接近，常用于才能。

entries.definition: Coming after the present; plainer and less tentative than prospective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「未来的」，比 prospective 平实，推测意味较少。

entries.definition: Looking back at what has already happened; the exact opposite of prospective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「回顾的、追溯的」，与 prospective 正好相反。

entries.definition: Probable; states the chance rather than the position in time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可能的」，说的是概率而非时间位置。

entries.definition: Hoping to become successful; it names the wish, not the expectation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有志成为的」，说的是愿望而非预期。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root, the preposition inside the word and the true opposite prefix.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根、词中藏着的介词，以及真正相对的前缀。

normal.en: specere is to look, so prospective is what you look at ahead.
normal.cn: specere 是「看」，prospective 就是你向前看时看到的东西。

normal.en: pro- means forward: the same pro- opens prospective and project.
normal.cn: pro- 意为「向前」，prospective 与 project 都带着这个前缀。

normal.en: retrospective looks back, prospective looks ahead.
normal.cn: retrospective 回头看，prospective 向前看。

normal.en: A prospective buyer is not yet a buyer.
normal.cn: prospective buyer 还不是买家。

normal.en: prospect is the noun, prospective is the adjective made from it.
normal.cn: prospect 是名词，prospective 是它派生出的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a road running forward to a house you have not reached yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一条向前延伸的路，尽头是一座你还没抵达的房子。

abstract.en: Picture a change written on a calendar page that is still months ahead.
abstract.cn: 想象一项变化写在还隔着好几个月的那页日历上。

abstract.en: Picture a law printed only for the documents filed after it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条只印给之后递交文件使用的法律。

examples.en: Prospective students can tour the campus during the open day.
examples.cn: 准新生可以在开放日参观校园。

examples.en: Several prospective buyers made offers on the flat within a week.
examples.cn: 一周内有几位潜在买家给这套公寓出价。

examples.en: The board discussed the prospective costs of the new branch.
examples.cn: 董事会讨论了新分店的预期成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普罗斯佩克提夫」——往「前」看（pro）到一「面」镜子（spect），镜中是未来的自己；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ specere（看）+ -ive（形容词后缀）→ prospectivus（向前看的、远景的）→ 英语 prospective，核心义「向前看时所见、尚未成真的」。

sensesIntro.en: Prospective always points forward: a person who may become something, an event that may happen, a law that works only ahead, and a list of things that may exist later.
sensesIntro.cn: prospective 始终朝前：可能成为某身份的人、可能发生的事、只管将来的法律，以及将来可能出现的事物清单。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road runs forward to a house that is not reached yet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条路伸向尚未抵达的房子。

branches.en: THE PERSON: someone expected to become a member later.
branches.cn: 人物线：预期以后会成为其中一员的人。

branches.en: THE EVENT: a change that is expected or planned to happen.
branches.cn: 事件线：预期或计划将要发生的变化。

branches.en: THE LAW: a rule that works only forward, never backward.
branches.cn: 法律线：只向将来生效、不追溯的规则。

branches.en: THE POSSIBLE: people and things that may exist but are not yet real.
branches.cn: 可能线：可能存在但尚未成真的人和事。

branches.en: THE VIEW: formal look at gains that may come.
branches.cn: 展望线：正式语境下对可能到来的收益的观望。

intro.en: Prospective is a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and an English adjective suffix joined in one word.
intro.cn: prospective 由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词词根和一个英语形容词后缀合成。

latinIntro.en: Latin has specere, prospectus and prospectivus as recorded words, so nothing in this family is invented.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中 specere、prospectus、prospectivus 都有文献记录，这一族词没有虚构的成分。

items.example: The prefix gives the sense of looking ahead.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给「向前看」的意思。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的词根。

items.example: It forms the noun part of prospectus.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 prospectus 中表示「景象」的部分。

items.example: It forms prospective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 prospective。

items.example: It forms prospectively.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 prospectively。

items.example: Prospect is the shorter noun.
items.exampleCN: prospect 是更短的名词。

items.example: The per- version gives us perspective.
items.exampleCN: 换用 per- 就成了 perspective。

items.example: The retro- form is its opposite.
items.exampleCN: retro- 形式是它的反面。

items.example: Prospective keeps the forward look.
items.exampleCN: prospective 保留「向前看」。

definition_zh: （招股）说明书；简介；课程简章；计划书
definition_en: a printed document that describes a company, a school or a project and its plans, given to people who may buy into it or join it
core_image: 一叠印好的小册子摊在桌上，第一页写着发行计划与前景
scene: 证券交易所的印刷室里，一摞摞小册子还带着油墨味，封面印着公司名与发行价，工作人员把它们装进给投资者的信封。Every investor received a thick prospectus before the public offering.
sceneCN: 这里 prospectus 是「招股说明书」（第 1 个义项：公司公开发行时说明情况的正式文件）；句意：每位投资者在公开发行前都收到了一本厚厚的招股说明书。画面里有印刷机、成摞的小册子和信封。

pos.zh: 名词：招股说明书；简介；课程简章；计划书

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁词构成，义为「前景；可能性」
由同一拉丁词构成，义为「预期的；未来的」
由同一词根加 -ion 构成，义为「远眺；勘查」，较少用
由同一词根加 -or 构成，义为「勘探者」

senses.title: A share issue document
senses.definition: a formal document issued by a company that offers shares or debt to the public, giving financial and business details required by law
senses.definitionCN: 公司向公众发行股票或债券时依法发布的正式文件，载明财务与经营细节
senses.example: Read the risk section of the prospectus before deciding to invest.
senses.exampleCN: 决定投资前先读一读招股说明书里的风险部分。
senses.why: Latin prospectus meant a wide view, and a document that opens up a firm to public view carries the same image: the company is laid out for investors to look over.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 prospectus 意为「开阔的视野」，把公司摊开给公众查看的文件延续了同一意象：公司被铺展开来供投资者打量。

senses.title: A school or course outline
senses.definition: a booklet that describes what a school or a course offers, its rules and its fees, given to parents or applicants
senses.definitionCN: 介绍学校或课程内容、规定与费用的小册子，发给家长或申请者
senses.example: The school prospectus lists every club and the uniform rules.
senses.exampleCN: 学校简介里列出了所有社团与校服规定。
senses.why: A school opens itself to families the way a company opens itself to investors, so the same booklet word is used for parents.
senses.whyCN: 学校向家庭展开自己的方式，与公司向投资者展开自己的方式一样，因此给家长看的册子用了同一个词。

senses.title: A project or business plan
senses.titleCN: 计划书；项目的说明文件
senses.definition: a document that sets out the purpose and the plan of a business, a charity or a proposed project
senses.definitionCN: 说明企业、慈善机构或拟议项目目的与计划的文件
senses.example: The charity sent a prospectus to donors describing the planned health centre.
senses.exampleCN: 慈善机构向捐赠者寄了一份计划书，介绍拟建的保健中心。
senses.why: A plan is a written prospect, and the document that shows it took the same name: what is laid out for the future is the plan itself.
senses.whyCN: 计划就是写下的一幅前景，展示它的文件沿用了同一名字：为未来铺展开的内容就是计划本身。

senses.title: A printed catalogue or syllabus
senses.definition: older or specialized use: a printed list or syllabus that announces what is on offer, such as a theatre season or a course of lectures
senses.definitionCN: 较旧或专门用法：宣布所提供的节目的印刷目录，如演出季预告或讲座课程大纲
senses.example: The theatre season prospectus was mailed to subscribers in August.
senses.exampleCN: 演出季的剧目介绍册在八月寄给了订户。
senses.why: Before the modern booklet there was a printed syllabus that announced a season of plays, and that older use survives.
senses.whyCN: 在现代小册子之前，已有宣布演出季的印刷大纲，这个较旧的用法保留了下来。

senses.title: Figurative: a view of what lies ahead
senses.definition: literary use: something that shows or opens up a view of what may happen next
senses.definitionCN: 文学用法：展现或展开未来可能发生之事的东西
senses.example: The new bridge is a prospectus of the trade the harbour hopes to attract.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新桥像是对未来贸易的一纸展望，港口正盼着那笔生意。
senses.why: At its oldest the Latin noun simply meant a wide view, so anything that opens up the future can borrow the word.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词最初只表示开阔的视野，因此凡是展开未来之势的事物都能借用这个词。

intro.en: Prospectus is a Latin noun for a view that took on the sense of a printed forecast and then of a document that sets out what is offered.
intro.cn: prospectus 本是拉丁语里表示「视野」的名词，后来带上印刷预告的含义，又引申为说明所提供内容的文件。

items.en: *spek- is generally reconstructed as to look, and it is the distant source of the Latin verb specere.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *spek- 表示「看」，它是拉丁语 specere 的远源。

items.en: From specere, to look, came spectus, a look or a sight, and with pro- the compound prospectus, a view or an outlook.
items.cn: 由 specere「看」生出 spectus「看、视野」，加上 pro- 构成 prospectus「眺望、远景」。

items.en: Neo-Latin writers used prospectus for a printed plan of a forthcoming book, and the sense of a public notice grew from that use.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的新拉丁语作者用 prospectus 指即将出版之书的印刷计划，表示公开通告的意义由此生长出来。

items.en: The word appears in English in the eighteenth century for plans of books and projects; the modern company and school uses developed in the following centuries. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 该词十八世纪出现在英语中，指书籍与项目的印刷计划；现代的公司与学校用法在此后几百年中形成。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Company law made the prospectus a regulated document, while schools and charities still print a plain prospectus for parents and donors.
items.cn: 公司法把 prospectus 变成受监管的正式文件，学校与慈善机构仍为家长和捐赠者印制普通的简介。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin noun for a view; the near-meaning group gathers the other documents printed before a decision.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语「视野」名词构成的词；近义组收在做出决定前印发的其他文书。

entries.definition: The shorter noun for an outlook or a possibility, from which the longer form grew.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「前景、可能性」，较短的形式，较长的写法由它生长出来。

entries.definition: The adjective for what is expected or likely to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「预期的、未来的」。

entries.definition: Clear to the understanding; built on the same verb for seeing through.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明白易懂的」，由同一「看透」动词构成。

entries.definition: A Latin-looking word with a similar ending, but built on another verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形似的拉丁词，结尾相近，但由另一个动词构成，词根不同。

entries.definition: The regular plural of the word, used in company filings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数形式，用于公司报送的文件中。

entries.definition: A thin booklet that advertises goods or services; lighter and less formal than a prospectus.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小册子、宣传册」，比 prospectus 更轻薄随意。

entries.definition: A list of items for sale or on show, item by item.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目录」，逐条列出待售或展出的东西。

entries.definition: The outline of topics in a course of study; a prospectus describes the whole school.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「教学大纲」，prospectus 介绍的是整所学校。

entries.definition: A short written summary of the facts for a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「简介、要点摘要」，供决策参考。

entries.definition: A printed notice sent to many people at once.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通告函」，一次寄给许多人的印刷通知。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb for looking, the near neighbours of the word and the places it is actually printed.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「看」动词、这个词的邻近词，以及它实际出现的地方。

normal.en: specere is to look, so a prospectus is a sheet on which the company is looked over.
normal.cn: specere 是「看」，prospectus 就是让人打量这家公司的那份纸。

normal.en: prospect is the short noun, prospective the adjective, prospectus the document.
normal.cn: prospect 是短名词，prospective 是形容词，prospectus 是文件。

normal.en: A share prospectus must be read before the money is paid.
normal.cn: share prospectus 必须在付款前读完。

normal.en: Schools send a prospectus to parents, companies file one with the market.
normal.cn: 学校给家长寄简介，公司则向市场报送说明书。

normal.en: The plural is prospectuses, not prospecti.
normal.cn: 复数写作 prospectuses，不是 prospecti。

abstract.en: Picture a thick booklet on a desk with the share plan on its first page.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上放着一本厚小册子，第一页写着发股计划。

abstract.en: Picture a slim booklet beside a school gate, listing clubs and uniform rules.
abstract.cn: 想象校门口一本薄薄的简介册，列着社团与校服规定。

abstract.en: Picture a charity letter with a paper plan for a building that does not exist yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一封慈善机构的信，附着一座尚未建成的建筑的图纸。

examples.en: The company filed its prospectus with the exchange last week.
examples.cn: 上周公司向交易所递交了招股说明书。

examples.en: Parents found the new fee policy in the term prospectus.
examples.cn: 家长们在学期简章里看到了新的收费政策。

examples.en: Every claim in the prospectus must be accurate and clear.
examples.cn: 说明书里的每一项表述都必须准确清晰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普罗斯佩克塔斯」——把公司摊在「前」面（pro）给人「看」（spect），摊开的正是这份说明书；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ specere（看）+ 名词词尾 -tus → prospectus（眺望、远景）→ 新拉丁语「出版计划」→ 英语 prospectus，核心义「把前景摊开给人看的文书」。

sensesIntro.en: Prospectus moves outward from the regulated share document to the school booklet, the project plan, the older printed outline, and at last a metaphor for a forecast.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从受监管的招股文件向外扩展到学校简章、项目计划、较旧的印刷目录，最后落到指前景展望的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a printed booklet lies open, and its first page sets out a plan and a future.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本翻开的小册子摆在桌上，首页写着计划与前景。

branches.en: THE MARKET: a company laid open for public investors.
branches.cn: 市场线：把公司摊开给公众投资者看。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: a booklet that opens the school to parents and applicants.
branches.cn: 学校线：把学校摊开给家长和申请者的简章。

branches.en: THE PROJECT: a plan of what a body intends to do.
branches.cn: 项目线：说明机构打算做什么的计划书。

branches.en: THE CATALOGUE: an older printed outline that announces what is on offer.
branches.cn: 目录线：较旧的印刷大纲，宣布所提供的内容。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: whatever opens a view of what may come.
branches.cn: 比喻线：凡是展开未来可能之势的事物。

intro.en: Prospectus is a Latin prefix, a Latin verb of seeing and a Latin noun ending, later borrowed into English as a whole word.
intro.cn: prospectus 由一个拉丁前缀、一个表示「看」的拉丁动词和一个拉丁名词词尾组成，后来整词借入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin has specere, spectus and prospectus as recorded forms, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中 specere、spectus、prospectus 都有文献记录，只有更早的印欧语词根属于重构。

items.example: The prefix turns looking into looking ahead.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「看」变成「向前看」。

items.example: The verb gives every word in this family its core.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给这一族每个词提供核心。

items.example: It joins the prefix to make prospectus.
items.exampleCN: 它与前缀结合构成 prospectus。

items.example: The ending makes a noun of the participle.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把分词变成名词。

items.example: It gives prospectuses.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 prospectuses。

items.example: Prospect is the short cousin.
items.exampleCN: prospect 是它的近亲短形式。

items.example: Perspective is made with another prefix.
items.exampleCN: 另一个前缀构成 perspective。

items.meaning: a person who searches for ore
items.example: A prospector searches for what lies ahead.
items.exampleCN: prospector 寻找前方地下的东西。

items.example: The -ion form names the looking.
items.exampleCN: 带 -ion 的形式指「看」这件事。

definition_zh: 繁荣；兴旺；成功；发达
definition_en: to grow strong and successful, especially in business or in personal fortunes
core_image: 田里的麦穗顺着风势越长越高，粒粒饱满
scene: 小镇的纺织厂重新开工后，商铺和住户都渐渐兴旺起来。After the old mill reopened, the whole town began to prosper again.
sceneCN: 这里 prosper 是「兴旺、繁荣」（第 1 个义项：经济或事业蒸蒸日上）；句意：老纺织厂重新开工后，整座小镇又开始兴旺起来。

pos.zh: 繁荣；兴旺；发达
使繁荣；使成功（书面语较少用）

collocations.zh: 在压力下反而发展得好

derivatives.zh: prosper 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，表示「繁荣；富足」的状态
prosper 加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，表示「繁荣的；富裕的」
prosperous 再加副词后缀 -ly，表示「兴旺地」

senses.title: To grow and thrive
senses.definition: to become stronger and more successful over time, of a place, business, or group
senses.definitionCN: 地方、生意或群体随着时间变得更强、更成功
senses.example: The port prospered for a century on the wool trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这个港口靠羊毛贸易繁荣了一个世纪。
senses.why: The Latin root means to succeed according to hope, and hope fulfilled shows up first as visible growth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「如所愿地成功」，愿望实现最直接的表现就是看得见的生长，所以义项落在「繁荣」上。

senses.title: To do well as a person
senses.definition: to become rich or successful in personal life or career
senses.definitionCN: 个人在生活或事业上变富、取得成功
senses.example: She prospered as a young architect in the new city.
senses.exampleCN: 她作为年轻建筑师在这座新城事业有成。
senses.why: When the growth belongs to one person rather than a place, the sense narrows to personal success.
senses.whyCN: 当这种增长属于某个人而不是某个地方时，义项就从群体的繁荣收窄为个人的发达与成功。

senses.title: To make others prosper
senses.definition: to cause someone or something to succeed, mainly in formal or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某事物成功昌盛，多用于正式或文学语境
senses.example: Could such a policy prosper the whole region?
senses.exampleCN: 这样的政策真能让整个地区繁荣起来吗？
senses.why: English lets the same verb take an object, so the cause of growth takes the place of growth itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许同一个动词带宾语，于是「带来增长的人或事」取代了「增长本身」，形成使动义项。

senses.title: To benefit from a situation
senses.definition: to gain an advantage from a particular condition or event
senses.definitionCN: 从某种条件或事件中获得好处而兴旺
senses.example: Small shops prospered from the new footbridge.
senses.exampleCN: 小店铺因这座新人行天桥而生意兴隆。
senses.why: Prospering always has a source, and the source sense makes the partner of the verb explicit.
senses.whyCN: 兴旺总有来源，这个义项把受益的来源明说出来，聚焦在「因何而得利」上。

senses.title: To do well under pressure
senses.titleCN: 在压力下反而发展得好
senses.definition: to develop well in conditions that would defeat others
senses.definitionCN: 在别人难以承受的条件下反而发展得好
senses.example: The hardy mountain herb prospers under frost.
senses.exampleCN: 这种耐寒的高山草本植物在霜冻中反而长得更好。
senses.why: The growth image can be used for anything that takes advantage of difficulty, including plants.
senses.whyCN: 「生长」这一意象可以投射到任何能借困境壮大的对象上，植物也是如此，于是有了「逆势兴旺」。

intro.en: Prosper comes from Latin prosper, meaning favourable or according to hope, a word whose own origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: prosper 源自拉丁语 prosper，意为「有利的、如愿的」，这个词本身的来源尚有争议。

items.en: A reconstructed root speh- is often proposed, but the link is not certain.
items.cn: 常有学者提出重构词根 speh-，但这一联系并不确定。

items.en: Prosper means favourable, cheering, or according to hope.
items.cn: 拉丁语 prosper 意为「有利的、令人欣喜的、如愿的」。

items.en: Prosperare means to succeed or make happy.
items.cn: 动词 prosperare 意为「成功、使顺利」。

items.en: English borrows the verb in the sense of doing well.
items.cn: 英语约在十五世纪借入该动词，表示「做得好、兴旺」。

items.en: The verb settles on economic and personal success.
items.cn: 现代英语中该动词稳定用于经济与个人事业的成功。

note.en: Prosper travels with its family of success words and neighbours the vocabulary of wealth and growth.
note.cn: prosper 与一组成败词同源同行，语义上又紧邻「财富与增长」一类词。

entries.definition: the state of being successful and wealthy
entries.definitionCN: 繁荣；富足

entries.definition: successful and rich
entries.definitionCN: 繁荣的；富裕的

entries.definition: likely to happen in the future
entries.definitionCN: 未来的；可能的；与 prosper 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to grow and become strong and healthy
entries.definitionCN: 茁壮成长；兴旺

entries.definition: to develop well and be very active
entries.definitionCN: 繁荣；蓬勃发展

entries.definition: to reach a goal or achieve what is wanted
entries.definitionCN: 成功

normalIntro.en: Prosper is a growth verb: from a favourable start, a thing keeps getting stronger.
normalIntro.cn: prosper 是一个表示生长的动词：从有利的起点出发，一路越长越壮。

normal.en: Prosperity is the noun; prosperous is the adjective built from the verb.
normal.cn: 名词是 prosperity，形容词 prosperous 也由这个动词派生。

normal.en: Businesses that adapt often prosper in hard times.
normal.cn: 善于调整生意的企业常能在艰难时期兴旺。

normal.en: A region can prosper from trade without any industry.
normal.cn: 一个地区不必有工业，靠贸易也能兴旺。

normal.en: Thrive and flourish are common partners of prosper in writing.
normal.cn: 在写作中 thrive 和 flourish 常与 prosper 并列使用。

normal.en: Do not confuse prosper with prospect, which means a view or a future chance.
normal.cn: 不要把 prosper 与 prospect 混淆，后者指「景象」或「前景」。

abstract.en: Picture wheat growing taller than the fence that was built around it.
abstract.cn: 想象麦子长得比围住它的篱笆还要高。

abstract.en: Imagine a shop that fills its shelves one row at a time each season.
abstract.cn: 想象一家店铺每个季节都把货架多摆满一排。

abstract.en: See a small sapling that two people once bent down, now a thick tree.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵曾被人压弯的小树苗，如今已长成粗壮的大树。

examples.en: Companies that invest early in green energy tend to prosper.
examples.cn: 早早投资绿色能源的公司往往能够兴旺。

examples.en: The fishing villages prospered once the new harbour was built.
examples.cn: 新港口建成后，这些渔村就繁荣起来。

examples.en: Few people prosper without a plan for the next decade.
examples.cn: 很少有人在没有未来十年计划的情况下发达。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑肉死」——拼了命往前扑，肉才能越积越多；这只是谐音画面，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、替……）+ sper（希望，词形存疑）→ prosperare（成功、使顺利）→ 古法语 prosperer → 英语 prosper，核心义「如所愿地向前走」。

sensesIntro.en: Prosper begins with the growth of a place or business, narrows to a person doing well, extends to making others succeed, and finally points to the source of the gain.
sensesIntro.cn: prosper 先指地方或生意的生长，再收窄为个人发达，进而指使他人成功，最后指向得利的来源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wheat rising above the fence that was meant to hold it back.
core.cn: 核心意象：麦子长得高过原本围住它的篱笆。

branches.en: A port or factory that keeps expanding.
branches.cn: 不断扩张的港口或工厂。

branches.en: A person whose career keeps climbing.
branches.cn: 事业一路向上的人。

branches.en: A policy that lifts a whole region.
branches.cn: 带动整个地区的政策。

branches.en: Trade, a bridge, or cheap power as the source of gain.
branches.cn: 贸易、桥梁或廉价电力作为得利来源。

branches.en: Growth that happens in unfriendly conditions.
branches.cn: 在不友好的条件下仍发生的增长。

intro.en: Prosper is a bare Latin verb with no suffix; the items below collect the prefix and suffix pieces that build its family and the vocabulary of growth.
intro.cn: prosper 本身是不带后缀的拉丁动词；下列条目汇集了构成它词族的词缀片段以及「生长」类词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin prosperare means to succeed, and its adjective prosper adds a hopeful sense to the growing image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prosperare 意为「成功」，其形容词 prosper 给生长意象加上「如愿」的色彩。

items.example: Prosper entered English as a verb.
items.exampleCN: prosper 以动词形式进入英语。

items.meaningCN: 构成第一变位法动词的词尾
items.example: Prosperare is the Latin infinitive.
items.exampleCN: prosperare 是拉丁语不定式。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms prosperity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 prosperity。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms prosperous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 prosperous。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms prosperously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 prosperously。

items.example: Prosperer is a rare word for a successful person.
items.exampleCN: prosperer 是少见的说法，指成功者。

items.example: Prospering towns attract young workers.
items.exampleCN: 繁荣的城镇吸引年轻工人。

items.example: Flourish shares the growth idea.
items.exampleCN: flourish 共享「生长」这一概念。

items.example: Thrive is a plain native partner of prosper.
items.exampleCN: thrive 是 prosper 常见的本族语近义词。

definition_zh: 伸出；突出；鼓出；探出
definition_en: to stick out from a surface or beyond a limit
core_image: 一颗钉子从木板里顶出来，尖端露在外面
scene: 行李箱塞得太满，一件毛衣从拉链缝里露了出来。A wool sweater protruded from the gap in the overstuffed suitcase.
sceneCN: 这里 protrude 是「伸出、露出来」（第 1 个义项：从表面向外突出）；句意：一件毛衣从塞得过满的行李箱缝里露了出来。

pos.zh: 伸出；突出；鼓出
使伸出；使突出（较少用）

derivatives.zh: protrude 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，表示「突出部分；突出」
protrude 加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，表示「突出的；伸出的」
过去分词作形容词，表示「露在外面的」

senses.title: To stick out from a surface
senses.definition: to extend outward from the surface around it
senses.definitionCN: 从周围的表面向外伸出
senses.example: A rusty nail protruded from the fence post.
senses.exampleCN: 一根生锈的钉子从篱笆柱上凸了出来。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to thrust forward, and pushing outward is exactly what makes a thing stick out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「向前推」，向外一推，就形成了从表面突出的样子，所以义项第一解释就是「伸出」。

senses.title: To bulge outward
senses.definition: to swell or press outward so that a full rounded shape appears
senses.definitionCN: 向外鼓起或撑出，形成圆鼓鼓的形状
senses.example: His eyes protruded in surprise.
senses.exampleCN: 他惊讶得眼珠都凸出来了。
senses.why: Pressure from inside also counts as thrusting, so the pushing image covers round swellings.
senses.whyCN: 从内部向外顶同样是一种「推」，所以推力意象也能覆盖圆鼓鼓的外凸形状。

senses.title: To reach beyond a boundary
senses.definition: to extend past a line, edge, or allowed space
senses.definitionCN: 超出某条线、某个边缘或允许的范围
senses.example: The balcony protruded over the narrow street.
senses.exampleCN: 阳台探出到狭窄的街道上方。
senses.why: Anything that is thrust forward can cross a limit, so the same verb names passing beyond an edge.
senses.whyCN: 被推向前的东西也可能越过界限，所以同一个动词也能表示超出某条边缘。

senses.title: To make something stick out
senses.definition: to cause an object to extend outward, mainly in technical writing
senses.definitionCN: 使物体向外伸出，多用于技术描写
senses.example: The engineer protruded the rod through the casing.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师让杆子穿出外壳。
senses.why: English allows the same verb to take an object, so the one who pushes takes the subject position.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许同一动词带宾语，于是「施加推力的人」占据主语位置，形成使动义项。

senses.title: To be noticeable
senses.definition: to be clearly visible because it stands out from its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 因为与周围不同而清楚显露
senses.example: One bright idea protruded from an otherwise dull report.
senses.exampleCN: 一份乏味的报告里，一个亮眼的观点格外突出。
senses.why: What sticks out is seen first, and that literal visibility becomes a metaphor for being striking.
senses.whyCN: 突出的东西最先被看见，这种字面上的「可见」自然延伸为比喻意义上的「引人注目」。

intro.en: Protrude comes from Latin protrudere, to thrust forward, built from pro- forward and trudere to push.
intro.cn: protrude 源自拉丁语 protrudere（向前推），由 pro-（向前）与 trudere（推）构成。

items.en: A reconstructed root treud- underlies the pushing family, though its exact shape is debated.
items.cn: 重构词根 treud- 是该「推」词族的基础，其确切形式仍有争论。

items.en: Trudere means to push or thrust; pro adds forward.
items.cn: trudere 意为「推、用力顶」；pro 加上「向前」。

items.en: Protrudere means to push forward or drive out.
items.cn: protrudere 意为「向前推、赶出去」。

items.en: English borrows protrude in the sense of thrusting out.
items.cn: 英语约在十七世纪借入 protrude，表示「推出、伸出」。

items.en: The verb becomes intransitive, and things simply stick out by themselves.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词多作不及物动词，描述物体自己突出来。

note.en: Protrude shares its pushing root with intrude and extrude, and sits beside the plain words for sticking out.
note.cn: protrude 与 intrude、extrude 共享「推」的词根，语义上又紧挨着表示「凸出」的普通词。

entries.definition: to enter a place where one is not wanted
entries.definitionCN: 侵入；闯入

entries.definition: to force material out through a shaped opening
entries.definitionCN: 挤出；挤压成形

entries.definition: something that sticks out
entries.definitionCN: 突出部分；突出

entries.definition: to swell outward in a rounded shape
entries.definitionCN: 鼓出；凸起

entries.definition: to extend beyond the surrounding surface
entries.definitionCN: 伸出；突出

entries.definition: to stick out beyond a surface
entries.definitionCN: 突出；伸出

normalIntro.en: Protrude is a pushing verb: pro- forward plus trudere to push.
normalIntro.cn: protrude 是表示「推」的动词：pro- 向前，加上 trudere 推。

normal.en: Intrude, extrude, and protrude all end in the same pushing root.
normal.cn: intrude、extrude、protrude 都以同一「推」词根结尾。

normal.en: Note the spelling trude, not tiude, before the ending.
normal.cn: 注意拼写是 trude，不是 tiude，t 后面接 r。

normal.en: Protruding is the common adjective form in descriptions of faces and machines.
normal.cn: protruding 是形容容貌与机器零件时常用的形容词形式。

normal.en: Rocks that protrude from the sea can wreck small boats.
normal.cn: 从海面突出的岩石能撞坏小船。

normal.en: Use stick out in speech and protrude in careful writing.
normal.cn: 口语用 stick out，严谨书面语用 protrude。

abstract.en: Picture a nail head standing proud of a plank of wood.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗钉头从木板上鼓出来。

abstract.en: Imagine a turtle poking its head out of the shell.
abstract.cn: 想象乌龟把头从壳里探出来。

abstract.en: See a rock ridge rising above the calm water.
abstract.cn: 想象一道岩脊露出平静的水面。

examples.en: Sharp metal edges protruded from the damaged door.
examples.cn: 损坏的门上露出锋利的金属边。

examples.en: The patient had a small protruding bone above the wrist.
examples.cn: 病人手腕上方有一小块突出的骨头。

examples.en: Do not let the wiring protrude through the insulation.
examples.cn: 不要让电线从绝缘层里露出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑着吐的」——被推得扑出来、吐到外面，就是「突出」；这只是谐音画面，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ trudere（推）→ protrudere（向前推）→ 英语 protrude，核心义「被推得向外顶出来」；同族有 intrude、extrude、abstruse。

sensesIntro.en: Protrude starts from a thing pushed outward from a surface, widens to round swellings, extends to crossing a boundary, gains a causative form, and finally becomes a metaphor for standing out.
sensesIntro.cn: protrude 从「被向外推而突出表面」出发，扩展到圆鼓的外凸、越界探出、使动用法，最后引申为「显眼」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nail pushed through a plank, its head standing outside the wood.
core.cn: 核心意象：被推出木板的钉子，钉头露在木头外面。

branches.en: A nail or rock edge beyond the surface.
branches.cn: 露出表面的钉子或岩石边缘。

branches.en: Rounded swelling pushed from inside.
branches.cn: 被内部顶出的圆形隆起。

branches.en: A balcony over the street line.
branches.cn: 越过街道界线的阳台。

branches.en: An engineer pushing a rod through a casing.
branches.cn: 工程师把杆子推穿外壳。

branches.en: What juts out is what the eye notices.
branches.cn: 凸出来的东西，正是眼睛最先注意到的。

intro.en: Protrude is built from a prefix and a pushing root, and the same root builds several English verbs of entry and exit.
intro.cn: protrude 由前缀加「推」词根构成，同一词根还构成英语中若干「进」「出」类动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pro- means forward and trudere means to push; together they shape protrudere and its relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pro- 意为「向前」，trudere 意为「推」，二者合起来塑造了 protrudere 及其同族词。

items.example: Pro- in protrudere marks forward movement.
items.exampleCN: protrudere 中的 pro- 表示向前。

items.example: The root trud- appears in intrude and extrude.
items.exampleCN: 词根 trud- 出现在 intrude 和 extrude 中。

items.example: In- plus trudere gives intrude.
items.exampleCN: in- 加 trudere 构成 intrude。

items.example: Ex- plus trudere gives extrude.
items.exampleCN: ex- 加 trudere 构成 extrude。

items.example: The suffix -sion forms protrusion.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -sion 构成 protrusion。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms protrusive.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 protrusive。

items.example: Protruding teeth can be corrected.
items.exampleCN: 外突的牙齿可以矫正。

items.example: A protruded bolt must be trimmed.
items.exampleCN: 凸出的螺栓必须削平。

items.example: Abstruse keeps the same pushing root.
items.exampleCN: abstruse 保留了同一「推」词根。

definition_zh: 有先见之明的；未雨绸缪的；节约的；提供……的
definition_en: showing care for the future, especially by saving and planning ahead
core_image: 入冬前把粮仓装满、把柴堆码好的人
scene: 老船长每次出海前都先备好淡水和药品，从不等到风暴来了才着急。The provident old captain stocked water and medicine before every voyage.
sceneCN: 这里 provident 是「未雨绸缪的、有远见的」（第 1 个义项：为将来提前做准备）；句意：这位未雨绸缪的老船长每次出海前都备好淡水和药品。

pos.zh: 未雨绸缪的；有先见之明的
节约的；节俭的
提供……的；供给的（与 of 连用）

collocations.zh: 对未来未雨绸缪的关照

derivatives.zh: provident 加名词后缀 -ence 构成，表示「远见；天意」
provident 加副词后缀 -ly，表示「有远见地；节俭地」
加否定前缀 im-，表示「无远见的；挥霍的」
只是拼写开头相近，来自 improve 而非 provide 的派生

senses.title: Planning ahead for needs
senses.definition: careful to prepare for what will be needed in the future
senses.definitionCN: 细心为将来的需要提前做准备
senses.example: Provident families store grain long before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 勤俭持家的家庭在入冬很久之前就存好粮食。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to see ahead, and seeing ahead naturally grows the image of preparing in advance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「预先看见」，预先看见自然而然地长成「提前准备」的意象，所以第一义项是未雨绸缪。

senses.title: Careful with money
senses.definition: thrifty, especially by putting money away for later
senses.definitionCN: 节省，尤指把钱存起来以备后用
senses.example: A provident worker saves part of every wage.
senses.exampleCN: 节俭的工人会存下每份工资的一部分。
senses.why: Saving is the everyday form of planning ahead, so applying the word to money gives the thrifty sense.
senses.whyCN: 储蓄是「提前准备」在日常生活中的具体形式，把这一特质用在钱上，就产生了「节俭」的义项。

senses.title: Supplying what is needed
senses.definition: furnishing or supplying something, used with of in older style
senses.definitionCN: 提供或供给某物，旧式用法中与 of 连用
senses.example: The grove was provident of shade on hot days.
senses.exampleCN: 那片树林在炎热的日子里提供了荫凉。
senses.why: The supplying verb underneath the adjective still shines through, so provident of means furnish with.
senses.whyCN: 形容词背后的「供给」动词义仍然透出，所以 provident of 就表示「备有、提供……」的意思。

senses.title: God as provider
senses.titleCN: 天意眷顾的；上天安排的
senses.definition: showing the care of Providence, in religious discourse
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教语境中体现天道的眷顾
senses.example: The islanders trusted a provident hand behind the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 岛民相信风暴背后自有上天的眷顾。
senses.why: Seeing ahead belongs to the divine eye too, so capital Providence lends the adjective a religious sense.
senses.whyCN: 「预先看见」也属于神的视域，大写 Providence 的用法让这个形容词带上了宗教色彩。

senses.title: Frugal use of resources
senses.definition: using natural or material resources carefully so that none is wasted
senses.definitionCN: 仔细使用自然或物质资源，不造成浪费
senses.example: Provident use of water keeps the garden alive in drought.
senses.exampleCN: 节约用水，才能在旱季保住园子。
senses.why: Thrift extends from money to any scarce resource, since careful use is also a kind of looking ahead.
senses.whyCN: 节俭从金钱扩展到任何稀缺资源，因为精打细算同样是一种为将来打算，于是有此义项。

intro.en: Provident comes from Latin providere, to see ahead or look after, built from pro- forward and videre to see.
intro.cn: provident 源自拉丁语 providere（预先看见、照看），由 pro-（向前）与 videre（看）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root weid- means to see or know.
items.cn: 重构词根 weid- 意为「看见、知道」。

items.en: Videre means to see, and pro- adds the idea of before.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，pro- 加上「在之前」的意思。

items.en: Providere means to foresee or to look after.
items.cn: providere 意为「预见」或「照看」。

items.en: Providens, the present participle, means foreseeing or careful.
items.cn: 现在分词 providens 意为「预见的、细心的」。

items.en: English borrows provident through French and Old French usage in the sense of thrifty or foreseeing.
items.cn: 英语经法语与古法语的用法借入 provident，表示「节俭的、有远见的」。

items.en: The adjective also names a government or employer fund set aside for future need.
items.cn: 现代英语中该形容词也用于指为将来需要而预留的政府或雇主基金。

note.en: Provident shares its seeing root with provide, evident, and vision, and sits opposite the words for careless spending.
note.cn: provident 与 provide、evident、vision 共享「看」的词根，语义上又与「挥霍」类词相对。

entries.definition: to give what is needed
entries.definitionCN: 提供；供给

entries.definition: foresight, or the care of a divine power
entries.definitionCN: 远见；天意

entries.definition: relating to a province
entries.definitionCN: 省的；地方的；与 provident 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: careful with money and resources
entries.definitionCN: 节俭的

entries.definition: showing care and thought for the future
entries.definitionCN: 审慎的；有远见的

entries.definition: lacking care for the future
entries.definitionCN: 不审慎的；轻率的

normalIntro.en: Provident is a seeing word: pro- forward plus videre to see, so it means seeing ahead.
normalIntro.cn: provident 是表示「看」的词：pro- 向前加 videre 看，合起来就是「事先看见」。

normal.en: Provident pairs with providence as noun and providently as adverb.
normal.cn: 名词是 providence，副词是 providently。

normal.en: Provident fund is the standard term for money set aside for retirement.
normal.cn: provident fund 是「公积金」的标准说法。

normal.en: The negative form is improvident, not unprovident.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 improvident，而不是 unprovident。

normal.en: Provident and provide share the same Latin verb, so thinking of provide helps.
normal.cn: provident 与 provide 同出一源，记住 provide 有助于记忆。

normal.en: Do not confuse provident with provincial, which means relating to a province.
normal.cn: 不要把 provident 与 provincial 混淆，后者指「省的、地方的」。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer filling the storehouse before the first frost.
abstract.cn: 想象一位农夫在初霜之前把粮仓填满。

abstract.en: Imagine a sailor tying spare ropes that no one will touch for months.
abstract.cn: 想象一位水手绑好几个月都用不上的备用绳索。

abstract.en: See a lamp lit at dusk by someone who has already checked the oil.
abstract.cn: 想象有人在黄昏点灯，而灯油早已检查过。

examples.en: Provident farmers feed the soil before it runs thin.
examples.cn: 有远见的农人会在土地变贫瘠之前养护它。

examples.en: The school keeps a provident fund for needy students.
examples.cn: 学校为贫困学生设有一项公积金。

examples.en: His provident habits let him retire ten years early.
examples.cn: 他节俭的习惯让他提前十年退休。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若喂等」——提前喂饱等着，就是「未雨绸缪」；这只是谐音画面，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ videre（看）→ providere（预先看见、照看）→ 现在分词 providens → 英语 provident，核心义「提前看见并准备好」；同族有 provide、providence、evident、vision。

sensesIntro.en: Provident begins with the general habit of preparing ahead, narrows to thrift with money, recovers its supplying force in a fixed phrase, and carries a divine and a resource-management sense.
sensesIntro.cn: provident 从「提前准备」的总体习惯出发，收窄为金钱上的节俭，又在其固定搭配中恢复「供给」本义，另有宗教与资源管理两个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a storehouse filled before the first frost, wood stacked and grain sealed.
core.cn: 核心意象：初霜之前已填满的粮仓，柴已码好，粮已封存。

branches.en: Grain stored before winter.
branches.cn: 入冬前就存好的粮食。

branches.en: Wages with a saved share.
branches.cn: 留出储蓄部分的工资。

branches.en: A grove that gives shade.
branches.cn: 提供荫凉的树林。

branches.en: A hand of Providence behind the storm.
branches.cn: 风暴背后的天意之手。

branches.en: Careful use of water and of wages.
branches.cn: 小心使用水和工资。

intro.en: Provident is a prefix plus a seeing root, and the words around it are all built on the same Latin idea of looking ahead.
intro.cn: provident 由前缀加「看」词根构成，围绕它的词也建立在「预先看」这一拉丁概念上。

latinIntro.en: Latin pro- means forward and videre means to see; their verb providere means to see ahead.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pro- 意为「向前」，videre 意为「看」，两词合成的 providere 意为「预先看见」。

items.example: Pro- in providere marks seeing before.
items.exampleCN: providere 中的 pro- 表示「事先」。

items.example: The root vid- also appears in evident and vision.
items.exampleCN: 词根 vid- 也出现在 evident 与 vision 中。

items.meaning: to see ahead, to look after
items.example: The stem pro-vid- gave both provide and provident.
items.exampleCN: 词干 pro-vid- 同时产生 provide 与 provident。

items.example: The suffix -ent forms provident.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ent 构成 provident。

items.example: The suffix -ence forms providence.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ence 构成 providence。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms providently.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 providently。

items.example: Im- plus provident gives improvident.
items.exampleCN: im- 加 provident 构成 improvident。

items.example: Provided is the participle of provide.
items.exampleCN: provided 是 provide 的过去分词。

items.example: Providentism is not a standard word and should be avoided.
items.exampleCN: providentism 不是标准词，应当避免使用。

definition_zh: 高超技艺；非凡才能；勇猛；英勇
definition_en: great skill at doing something, or great bravery and strength, especially shown in battle
core_image: 战场上一名武士挺身而出，刀光与喝彩同时落下
scene: 比赛只剩最后几秒，全场屏息看他起跳扣篮。His athletic prowess won loud cheers from the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 prowess 是「高超技艺、非凡才能」（第 1 个义项：在技能或体能上的出类拔萃）；句意：他高超的运动才能赢得了全场观众的喝彩。

pos.zh: 高超技艺；非凡才能
勇猛；英勇

derivatives.zh: 古法语词干在英语中的残留形容词，义为「勇敢的、杰出的」，现已罕用
与 prowess 同源于古法语词干 prou；义为「自豪的；骄傲的」
proud + -ly 构成的副词，义为「自豪地；骄傲地」
由古英语 prid 发展而来，与 prowess 词源不同；义为「自豪；骄傲」

senses.title: Exceptional skill or ability in doing something
senses.definition: outstanding skill, talent, or competence in a particular activity, often watched and admired by others
senses.definitionCN: 在某一活动中表现出的出众技能、才华或能力，常被人观看和称赞
senses.example: Her prowess on the piano astonishes every audience.
senses.exampleCN: 她在钢琴上的高超技艺令每场观众惊叹。
senses.why: The word was formed from the Old French stem prou, meaning brave and worthy, so prowess means being outstandingly good, and modern use moves from battlefield to stage.
senses.whyCN: 该词由古法语词干 prou（勇敢、杰出）构成，本义是「出类拔萃」；现代用法从战场挪到了舞台与赛场，于是由「勇字当先」转成「技艺超群」。

senses.title: Valour and strength shown in battle
senses.definition: great bravery, physical strength, and fighting spirit, especially displayed in war or combat
senses.definitionCN: 尤其在战争或格斗中表现出的英勇、体力和斗志
senses.example: The young knight proved his prowess in the first battle.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻骑士在首战中证明了自己的勇猛。
senses.why: Prowess was first a chivalric term on the battlefield, and the brave gallant meaning of the Old French stem survives in that earliest sense.
senses.whyCN: prowess 最早是战场上的骑士用语，古法语词干「英勇」的含义就残存在这个最古老的义项里。

intro.en: Prowess comes through Middle English from Old French, built on the stem prou, brave and worthy, with the noun ending -esse.
intro.cn: prowess 经由中古英语来自古法语，由表示「勇敢、杰出」的词干 prou 加上名词词尾 -esse 构成。

items.en: Latin prodesse, to be useful, is a likely ancestor of the French stem prou.
items.cn: 拉丁语 prodesse（有用、有益）被认为是法语词干 prou 的可能祖先。

items.en: The adjective prou means brave, worthy, or gallant.
items.cn: 古法语形容词 prou 意为勇敢、可敬、英勇。

items.en: Proesce names valour and strength in battle.
items.cn: proesce 指战场上的勇敢与力量。

items.en: The borrowed form prowess keeps the chivalric sense of brave deeds.
items.cn: 借入英语的 prowess 保留了骑士式的「英勇事迹」之义。

items.en: Skilled writers widen the word to mean excellence in any art.
items.cn: 近代早期英语中，熟练的写作者把词义扩展到任何一种艺术上的卓越。

items.en: Today the word is mostly uncountable and used for remarkable skill.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词基本不可数，主要表示出众的技能。

note.en: Prowess sits beside the French braver stems and beside braveries like valour, skill, and excellence.
note.cn: prowess 一面挨着来自法语的「勇敢」词族，一面挨着 valour、skill、excellence 这类近义词。

entries.definition: brave, worthy, or gallant in Old French
entries.definitionCN: 古法语词，意为勇敢、可敬；其词干是英语 prowess 的直接来源

entries.definition: feeling pleased about achievements, or having too high an opinion of oneself
entries.definitionCN: 骄傲的；自豪的——与 prowess 共享「出众」这一核心意象

entries.definition: bravely or gallantly, a rare adverb left from the old stem
entries.definitionCN: 勇敢地——由旧词干留下的罕见副词

entries.definition: great bravery, especially in battle
entries.definitionCN: 英勇；勇猛（尤其指战斗中）

entries.definition: the ability to do something well, especially through training
entries.definitionCN: 技能；本领

entries.definition: expert professional knowledge or skill
entries.definitionCN: 专业知识；专门技能

normalIntro.en: Prowess keeps a French stem that meant brave, so the word carries both skill and courage.
normalIntro.cn: prowess 保留了一个意为「勇敢」的法语词干，因此同时带着技能与勇气两层意思。

normal.en: Athletic prowess is the skill of a superb athlete.
normal.cn: athletic prowess 就是一名出色运动员的技能。

normal.en: Military prowess means strength and skill in war.
normal.cn: military prowess 指战争中的实力与本领。

normal.en: To demonstrate prowess is to show off real competence.
normal.cn: demonstrate prowess 就是展示真正的本领。

normal.en: The -ess ending makes prowess an abstract noun, like largess.
normal.cn: -ess 词尾让 prowess 成为抽象名词，与 largess 同型。

normal.en: Compare valour, which keeps only the brave side of prowess.
normal.cn: 对比 valour：它只保留了 prowess 中「勇」的一面。

abstract.en: Picture a harp player whose hands move faster than the eye can follow.
abstract.cn: 想象一位竖琴师，双手快得眼睛都跟不上。

abstract.en: Imagine a helmeted knight raising a sword before a cheering crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一名戴盔骑士在欢呼的人群前举剑。

abstract.en: See a scoreboard lighting up as a single name is called.
abstract.cn: 想象计分板亮起，一个名字被念出来。

examples.en: The team has shown remarkable prowess in defence this season.
examples.cn: 本赛季球队在防守上展现出非凡的实力。

examples.en: Medieval tales praised the prowess of knights.
examples.cn: 中世纪的故事赞美骑士们的英勇。

examples.en: Engineers admired the prowess of the ancient builders.
examples.cn: 工程师们钦佩古代建造者的高超技艺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑绕死」——身手敏捷、敢扑敢缠，一看就是真本事；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 prou（勇敢、杰出）＋词尾 -esse → proesce → 中古英语 prowess，核心义「出众得令人称赞」。

sensesIntro.en: Prowess first means outstanding skill in any activity, then the bravery and strength once praised in battle.
sensesIntro.cn: prowess 先指在任何活动中出众的技能，再指昔日战场上被赞颂的勇敢与力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warrior stepping forward while a crowd watches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一名武士在众人注视中挺身而出。

branches.en: Outstanding skill is the modern and most frequent sense.
branches.cn: 出众技能是现代最常用的义项。

branches.en: Valour in battle is the original heroic sense.
branches.cn: 战场上的勇猛是最初的英雄式义项。

branches.en: Both the champion and the knight are admired for being outstandingly good.
branches.cn: 冠军与骑士都因出众而被赞赏。

branches.en: The battlefield sense of the oldest item keeps the chivalric flavour alive.
branches.cn: 最古老义项中的战场用法让骑士色彩延续至今。

branches.en: Skill on a court and courage in a fight share the same admiration.
branches.cn: 球场上的技艺与战斗中的勇气获得同样的赞叹。

intro.en: Prowess is a French borrow built on the stem prou and the abstract noun ending -ess.
intro.cn: prowess 是法语借词，由词干 prou 与抽象名词词尾 -ess 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin prodesse, to be useful, is a probable ancestor of the French stem prou.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prodesse（有用、有益）被认为是法语词干 prou 的可能祖先。

items.example: Prou supplies the core sense of the word.
items.exampleCN: prou 提供了该词的核心含义。

items.example: The ending -ess turns a quality into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ess 把某种性质变成名词。

items.example: Proesce is the direct Old French source.
items.exampleCN: proesce 是直接的古法语来源。

items.example: Prowess keeps the abstract noun sense.
items.exampleCN: prowess 保留了抽象名词的含义。

items.example: Proud shares the same Old French stem.
items.exampleCN: proud 共享同一个古法语词干。

items.example: The suffix -ness builds proudness from proud.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 由 proud 构成 proudness。

items.example: Proudness is a rare near relative.
items.exampleCN: proudness 是罕见的近亲词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms prowly from the old stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 由旧词干构成 prowly。

items.example: Prowly now survives only in older texts.
items.exampleCN: prowly 如今只见于较早的文本。

items.example: Prow is a rare survivor of the stem.
items.exampleCN: prow 是该词干罕见的残留形式。

latinEntries.example: Prodes is a probable link to the French stem.
latinEntries.exampleCN: prodes 可能是通往法语词干的环节。

definition_zh: 接近；邻近；接近度；附近
definition_en: the state of being near to someone or something in space, time, or relationship
core_image: 两盏灯挨得很近，光圈几乎交叠在一起
scene: 新诊所开在了老居民区旁，步行几分钟就到。The school was chosen for its proximity to the library.
sceneCN: 这里 proximity 是「邻近、靠近」（第 1 个义项：在空间上离得很近）；句意：这所学校之所以被选中，是因为它离图书馆很近。

pos.zh: 接近；邻近；接近度

collocations.zh: 物理上的接近；身体上的靠近

derivatives.zh: proxim + -ate 构成的形容词，义为「最近的；直接的」
proxim + -al 构成的形容词，义为「近端的；近侧的」，常用于医学与解剖学
ap-（朝向）+ proxim + -ate，义为「近似的；接近」，是 proximity 在英语中最常见的同根词

senses.title: Nearness in space
senses.definition: the state of being physically near to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 在物理位置上离某人或某物很近的状态
senses.example: The hotel is popular because of its proximity to the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店因为离海滩近而受欢迎。
senses.why: The Latin superlative proximus means nearest, so the abstract noun names exactly the condition of being nearest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语最高级 proximus 意为「最近的」，由它构成的抽象名词，所指正是「处于最近」这一状态。

senses.title: Closeness in time or sequence
senses.definition: the fact of two events or periods following each other closely in time
senses.definitionCN: 两个事件或时期在时间上紧挨着发生的事实
senses.example: The proximity of the two elections worried the planners.
senses.exampleCN: 两次选举时间挨得太近，让规划者很担心。
senses.why: Nearest can describe moments as well as places, so the same abstract noun is applied to dates that fall close together.
senses.whyCN: 「最近」既能形容地点，也能形容时刻，因此同一个抽象名词被用来描述挨得很近的日期。

senses.title: Closeness in relationship or similarity
senses.titleCN: 亲疏关系上的接近；近似
senses.definition: the state of being closely related to something, or of being very similar in nature
senses.definitionCN: 与某事物关系密切，或在性质上非常相似的状态
senses.example: The proximity of the two theories makes them easy to confuse.
senses.exampleCN: 两种理论很接近，容易被人混淆。
senses.why: Similar or related things can be thought of as standing near each other in a conceptual space, so nearness becomes resemblance.
senses.whyCN: 性质相似或关系密切的事物，可以被想象成在概念空间里彼此挨着，于是「近」就转成了「相似」。

senses.title: Measured distance or nearness
senses.definition: the actual distance between two points, or the degree to which things are close
senses.definitionCN: 两点之间的实际距离，或事物彼此靠近的程度
senses.example: Sensors measure the proximity of the aircraft.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器测量飞机的接近距离。
senses.why: Once nearness is treated as a quantity, the noun can name a measured distance or degree on instruments.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把「近」当成一种量，这个词就能指仪器测得的距离或接近程度。

senses.title: Being in the neighbourhood
senses.definition: the local area around a place, considered as an accessible neighbourhood
senses.definitionCN: 某地周围的区域，被视为可以到达的附近地点
senses.example: We chose the flat for the proximity of shops and schools.
senses.exampleCN: 我们选择这套公寓，是因为附近有商店和学校。
senses.why: What lies near a place is its neighbourhood, so the state word comes to stand for that surrounding area.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方附近的一切就是它的周边，于是这个表状态的词转而指代那一片区域。

intro.en: Proximity comes from Latin proximus, the superlative of prope, near, plus the abstract noun ending -itas.
intro.cn: proximity 来自拉丁语 proximus（prope 的最高级，意为「近」），加上抽象名词词尾 -itas。
